observed.title: Headroom — Make room for your model
headings: From an OOMto an evidence trail.
What a report can tell you
observed.text:
Skip to content
headroom
Workspace
Results
About

A SMALLER MEMORY FOOTPRINT. A CLEARER EXPLANATION.

From an OOM
to an evidence trail.

Headroom investigates GPU memory in single-GPU PyTorch workloads, proposes a focused change, and checks what happened when the workload runs again.

Powered by NVIDIA Nemotron 3 on Nebius Token Factory
Research by Tavily
01 / LAB
Capture

Isolated runs record allocator history, stack traces, peak counters, and losses.

02 / REASON
Diagnose

Nemotron connects runtime evidence to source code and a constrained repair plan.

03 / PROPOSE
Patch

Changes stay in a separate copy, with policy checks and a readable diff.

04 / LAB
Verify

Measured memory, timing, loss behavior, and parameter counts determine the result.

NEBIUS TOKEN FACTORY

The model roles
Nemotron Ultra
Diagnosis and planning

Reads the evidence bundle and proposes causes and repairs with evidence references.

Nemotron Super
Patch generation

Produces a constrained diff for the selected plan, followed by static checks and verification.

Nemotron Nano
Allocation annotation

Intended for compact stack labels when that feature is available. Its use is recorded per run.

Tavily
Version-aware research

Finds official documentation and known issues. Retrieved content remains untrusted evidence.

BOUNDARIES MATTER

What a report can tell you
Static checks are guardrails, not a proof that arbitrary Python is safe or equivalent.
A memory snapshot explains observed allocations. A reserved-minus-allocated gap alone does not prove harmful fragmentation.
A proposed change is not a verified repair. Numerical comparisons may be unavailable, and precision changes must be explicit.
Missing usage data leaves cost unknown. A known subtotal is never represented as the final total.
Saved replays are historical records. Offline fixtures are marked and do not establish a successful model repair.
Current scope is single-GPU PyTorch. Long-context capacity, model features, and deployment readiness require their own acceptance evidence.

RELATED TOOLS

Built on existing work

PyTorch memory snapshots and memory_viz provide allocator inspection. Activation checkpointing, mixed precision, optimizer changes, and allocator configuration are established techniques. Headroom brings their investigation, a proposed source change, and measured verification into one reviewable workflow.

PyTorch memory snapshots
Activation checkpointing
Nebius Token Factory
